topPerforming.title: The $1,400 Bathroom Leak and the 90-Second Rule
topPerforming.whyItWorked: Relatable contractor loss aversion hook. Framing the missed call as an immediate $1,400 job lost resonates powerfully with emergency tradesmen.

topPerforming.title: Why You Miss Calls Mid-Fade: Barber & Salon Speed-to-Lead
topPerforming.whyItWorked: Visceral physical trade dilemma ('soapy hands / shears in hand cannot touch screen'). Non-techie audience immediately visualized their daily friction.

worstPerforming.title: Understanding Event-Driven Local Telephony daemons
worstPerforming.whyItFailed: Too much technical jargon ('telephony daemons', 'reconciliation buffers'). Contractors disengage when copy sounds like a software developer speaking.

algorithmLearnings: Rule 1: Always anchor the hook around an emergency jobsite scenario or physical obstruction (gloves, crawlspace, loud tools).
Rule 2: Eliminate all developer jargon. Replace 'carrier API / webhook' with 'your own phone number and carrier SIM'.
Rule 3: Video reels showing the real-time split screen of a homeowner dialing competitor vs getting an instant text achieve 2.8x higher watch completion.
Rule 4: Zero hashtags and zero emojis preserve an authentic peer-to-peer recommendation feel.
